title: Knowledge-Guided Generative Re-Stylization of CIM Models with Feature Continuance
authors: Y. Zhang; Y. Du; W. Chen; Z. Song; Q. Ping; B. Zhang; Y. Zhang; Y. Lv; X. Huang
source_title: 2025 6th International Conference on Computers and Artificial Intelligence Technology (CAIT)
abstract: City Information Modeling (CIM) serves as the digital bedrock for smart cities but faces a critical dilemma: high-fidelity 3D models inherently expose sensitive information, limiting multi-party data sharing. Existing desensitization methods, such as visual obfuscation or procedural replacement, sacrifice visual realism and semantic integrity for security. To resolve this, we propose a novel paradigm: “Knowledge-Guided Feature-Continuous Regeneration.” Rather than modifying original data, our approach abstracts a building into a structured “visual knowledge fingerprint,” which serves as a genetic blueprint to generate entirely new digital assets. We introduce a four-stage hybrid AI pipeline—Deconstruct-Generate-Reconstruct-Render—leveraging a purpose-built architectural layout generation model (Arch-Layout LoRA) and a knowledge-driven procedural engine. Experiments demonstrate that this method generates photorealistic, diverse, and architecturally valid models that sever the link to sensitive source data while controllably inheriting macro-style and semantic features. This work provides a “usable-but-unseen” security solution, transforming single data sources into diverse digital assets for the CIM ecosystem.

title: GrowSplat: Constructing Temporal Digital Twins of Plants with Gaussian Splats
authors: S. Adebola; S. Xie; C. M. Kim; J. Kerr; B. M. van Marrewijk; M. van Vlaardingen; T. van Daalen; E. N. van Loo; J. L. Susa Rincon; E. Solowjow; R. van Zedde; K. Goldberg

abstract: Accurate temporal reconstructions of plant growth can be valuable for plant phenotyping and breeding, yet remain challenging due to complex geometries, occlusions, and non-rigid deformations of plants. We present GrowSplat, a novel framework for building temporal digital twins of plants by combining 3D Gaussian Splatting with a robust spatial alignment pipeline. GrowSplat begins by constructing a temporal sequence of Gaussian Splats from multi-view camera data, then performs a two-stage spatial registration approach: coarse alignment through feature-based matching and Fast Global Registration, followed by fine alignment with Iterative Closest Point. This pipeline yields a consistent 4D model of plant development in discrete time steps. We evaluate the approach on data from the Netherlands Plant Eco-phenotyping Center, demonstrating detailed temporal reconstructions of Sequoia and Quinoa species. Videos and Images can be seen at https://berkeleyautomation.github.io/GrowSplat/

abstract: In applications like mobile surveying and digital twins, high-fidelity texturing of 3D LiDAR point clouds is crucial. Coloring points using panoramic images is effective, but occlusion artifacts occur when points at different depths project to the same pixel, incorrectly coloring distant points (e.g., a building) with textures from foreground objects (e.g., trees). This significantly reduces visual quality and reliability. To address this, we present an occlusion elimination method using multi-level filtering and grayscale matching. Compared to traditional methods or data-intensive deep learning approaches, our framework is computationally efficient, avoids the need for annotated training data, and achieves high accuracy.

abstract: Facing the urgent needs of national strategies such as “traffic power” and “new infrastructure” for the industrialization, intelligence and greening of bridges, this paper systematically puts forward the key technologies of intelligent monitoring and control system integrating “perception-decision-execution” around the goals of high precision, high efficiency and high safety in the construction of large-section bridge-building machines. Firstly, a monitoring framework for multi-sourccoordinate system and construction coordinate system, microsecond clock synchronization of PTP (Precision Time Protocol) and Adaptive Kalman Filter (AKF), high-precision alignment and optimal fusion of multi-source data such as lidar, fiber grating, inertial measurement unit (IMU) and GNSS in space and time dimensions are realized, and the comprehensive positioning accuracy after fusion is $\mathbf{\pm 1. 1 ~ m m}$; Secondly, based on model predictive control (MPC), a dynamic closed-loop control mechanism is established, aiming at the optimization of segmental beam line shape, embedding physical safety constraints such as hydraulic speed and pressure, and adopting rolling optimization and real-time feedback correction, the response time of calibration displacement is shortened by 74.4%, the hydraulic synchronization error is reduced by 74.3%, and the energy consumption is reduced by 28.3%. abstract: Digitizing physical objects into the virtual world has the potential to unlock new research and applications in embodied AI and mixed reality. This work focuses on recreating interactive digital twins of real-world articulated objects, which can be directly imported into virtual environments. We introduce Ditto to learn articulation model estimation and 3D geometry reconstruction of an articulated object through interactive perception. Given a pair of visual observations of an articulated object before and after interaction, Ditto reconstructs part-level geometry and estimates the articulation model of the object. We employ implicit neural representations for joint geometry and articulation modeling. Our experiments show that Ditto effectively builds digital twins of articulated objects in a category-agnostic way. title: mmDiff: A Noise-Robust Differentiable Ray-Tracing Framework for mmWave Scene Calibration and Channel Prediction
authors: H. Lu; Y. Cao; W. Yi; O. Abari
source_title: 2026 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition- FINDINGS Track (CVPRF)
abstract: 3D reconstruction techniques such as LiDAR scanning and photogrammetry have made it practical to build detailed geometric models of real-world environments. Such reconstructed models can potentially serve as the foundation for wireless digital twins and support network planning and optimization. The core challenge is that reconstructed models inevitably contain geometric artifacts such as holes and noisy surfaces, and wireless simulation is highly sensitive to such noise. To solve this problem, we propose a differentiable directional scattering model to approximate the noise-sensitive specular reflection. This approximation smoothly distributes reflected power among nearby ray directions, making the simulator inherently robust to local geometric artifacts in the reconstructed model. We prove mathematically that this approximation preserves asymptotic path-gain accuracy. Building on this idea, we propose mmDiff, an end-to-end differentiable framework for calibrating material properties from sparse mmWave measurements and predicting mmWave channels. We evaluate mmDiff on both real-world and synthetic datasets, and demonstrate its superior performance over prior methods using pure specular reflection in noisy reconstructed geometry. We open-source our implementation at https://github.com/LuHaofan/mmDiff.

title: OpenGERT: Open Source Automated Geometry Extraction with Geometric and Electromagnetic Sensitivity Analyses for Ray-Tracing Propagation Models
authors: S. Tadik; R. Bhattacharjea; J. Corgan; D. Johnson; J. Van der Merwe; G. D. Durgin
source_title: 2025 IEEE International Symposium on Dynamic Spectrum Access Networks (DySPAN)
abstract: Accurate RF propagation modeling in urban environments is crucial for developing high-fidelity digital spectrum twins and optimizing wireless communication systems. This paper introduces OpenGERT, an open-source automated Geometry Extraction tool for Ray Tracing. OpenGERT automates the collection and processing of terrain and building data from multiple sources, including OpenStreetMap, Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints, and USGS terrain elevation data. Leveraging the Blender Python API, the tool creates detailed urban models necessary for high-fidelity ray-tracing simulations specifically designed for NVIDIA Sionna RT. Moreover, we conduct sensitivity analyses to assess the impact of variations in building height, position, and electromagnetic material properties on the accuracy of ray-tracing models. Specifically, we present pairwise dispersion plots of channel statistics—such as path gain, mean excess delay, delay spread, link outage, and Rician K-factor—in response to perturbations to analyze the covariance of different channel statistics. The analyses also explore how the sensitivities of these statistics change as a function of distance from the transmitters. Additionally, we provide visualizations of the variance of the channel statistics within the scene for selected transmitter locations to offer deeper insights. Our study reports results from the Munich and Etoile scenes, each featuring 10 transmitter locations. For each transmitter location, we apply perturbations across five different types, 50 perturbations for each: material, position, height, height and position combined, and all combined. The findings reveal that, assuming the initial material properties of buildings are roughly accurate, minor perturbations in permittivity and conductivity do not significantly alter the channel statistics. In contrast, variations in building height and position have a considerable impact on all the statistics, even with a noise standard deviation of 1 meter for building heights and 0.4 meters for building positions. These results highlight the importance of precise environmental modeling in achieving reliable propagation predictions, which are essential for the deployment of digital spectrum twins and advanced communication networks. Finally, we share the code for geometry extraction and sensitivity analyses at https://github.com/serhatadik/OpenGERT/ to facilitate further experimentation and development.

title: Security-Aware Geometrically Robust 3D Watermarking: Threat Models, Games, and Evaluation Protocols
authors: Djumanov J.; Khudayberganov T.; Ibrohimova Z.; Raxmanov R.; Uralov J.; Umarov E.
source_title: International Conference of Young Specialists on Micro/Nanotechnologies and Electron Devices, EDM
abstract: Geometrically robust 3D watermarking is a practical mechanism for protecting digital graphical assets used in CAD/CAM, entertainment pipelines, digital twins, and additive manufacturing. However, many works still equate 'robustness' with survival under routine processing (e.g., smoothing or decimation) and rarely specify what an adaptive adversary can observe, query, or optimize. Building on a review of spectral-geometric invariants under realistic 3D acquisition distortions, this paper proposes a security-aware blueprint for evaluating and designing robust 3D watermarks under explicit threat assumptions. We contribute three methodological layers. First, we formalize a threat model capturing representation changes (mesh ↔ point cloud), acquisition-reconstruction loops, oracle access to embedding or detection services, collusion across many samples, and a utility constraint that prevents trivial 'removal by destruction.' Second, we introduce gamebased security definitions for removal, forgery, ambiguity, payload manipulation, and key recovery, with measurable adversarial advantages at a fixed detector operating point (controlled false-alarm rate). Third, we propose a parameterized attack taxonomy and a reproducible attacklibrary interface supporting composed attacks, adaptive score minimization, and standardized metadata logging. The resulting protocol reports both robustness curves (TPR/BER vs. attack strength) and security curves (e.g., key-recovery advantage vs. the number of observed assets). We illustrate the blueprint on spectral-geometric invariant watermarking, highlighting eigenbasis drift under remeshing/reconstruction and key-leakage risks under key reuse. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Automated Progress Monitoring of Power Infrastructure Construction via YOLOv8 Detection, Iterative Closest Point Alignment, and BIM Integration
authors: Xiao Y.
source_title: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy Systems and Power Engineering, EESPE 2026
abstract: Accurate and timely progress monitoring of power infrastructure construction sites, including substations, wind turbine foundations, photovoltaic mounting arrays, and transmission tower assemblies, is essential for grid commissioning schedules and for safety critical quality control. Traditional manual inspection is slow, costly, and subjective. This work presents a computer vision and Building Information Modeling integration framework that replaces fully image based three dimensional reconstruction with a feature level pipeline of YOLOv8 detection, structure from motion keypoint recovery, and Iterative Closest Point registration to the BIM reference model. The iterative optimization of the rigid transform is formulated explicitly, and geometric and temporal deviation metrics are defined with associated confidence intervals. Experiments are conducted on a multi site dataset of 15,360 labeled images collected from a 220 kV substation, an onshore wind farm, and a 50 MW photovoltaic plant, with controlled diversity in lighting, occlusion, and viewpoint. The proposed pipeline attains a mean average precision at intersection over union 0.5 of 0.942, an average alignment error of 17.6 mm, and a project level schedule deviation index of 2.9 percent. A paired comparison against Mask R CNN, Faster R CNN, and SSD baselines shows statistically significant gains at the 0.01 level. Relative to manual inspection, the pipeline reduces daily labor from 180 to 45 minutes per site and reduces absolute deviation error from 6.5 percent to 2.9 percent. The framework targets digital twin integration of energy infrastructure and supports smart grid commissioning workflows. © 2026 IEEE.

title: FedMamba-Twin: A Federated Mixture-of-State-Space-Experts Framework for Physics-Informed Multimodal Digital Twins in Earth Observation
authors: S. Mondal; S. Chopdar; A. Bajaj; M. Kumar; K. V; R. Kammari
source_title: 2026 10th International Conference on I-SMAC (IoT in Social, Mobile, Analytics and Cloud) (I-SMAC)
abstract: Earth observation (EO) increasingly relies on continuously updated digital twins that fuse optical, synthetic-aperture radar (SAR), thermal, and in-situ sensor streams to represent land, water, and atmosphere states in near real time. Building such twins collaboratively across space agencies, national ground segments, and commercial constellations is obstructed by data-sovereignty constraints that forbid raw-imagery sharing, by severe non-independent and identically-distributed (non-IID) heterogeneity across regions as well as sensors, and by the bandwidth limits of satellite and edge links. Existing federated learning (FL) methods for remote sensing address heterogeneity or communication efficiency in isolation, and existing EO foundation models assume centralized pretraining; neither line of work equips a federated twin with physical-consistency guarantees or calibrated confidence in its state estimates. We propose FedMamba-Twin, a federated framework that (i) equips each client with a frozen Mixture-of-State-Space-Experts (Fed-MoSSE) backbone built on selective state-space (Mamba-2) blocks for linear-time multimodal, multi-temporal fusion, personalized through communication-efficient low-rank adapters; (ii) attaches a physics-informed neural-operator head that constrains twin-state updates to satisfy conservation laws (e.g., surface energy balance) via a differentiable partial-differential-equation (PDE) residual loss; (iii) equips every client and the global twin with evidential uncertainty estimation calibrated by split-conformal prediction, giving distribution-free coverage guarantees on twin-state predictions; and (iv) aggregates client updates through an uncertainty-guided, communication-sparse weighting rule rather than uniform averaging. On a newly assembled five-modality, 24-client, non-IID EO benchmark (FedEO-Twin Bench), FedMamba-Twin improves global segmentation mIoU by 5.5–16.7 points over federated foundation-model and Mamba baselines while cutting per-client uplink cost by 60–87%, and it is the only evaluated method whose conformal intervals achieve near-nominal coverage across all tested confidence levels. To the best of our knowledge, no previous published study has combined conformal uncertainty quantification, physics-informed digital-twin state estimation, and state-space mixture-of-experts foundation models for multimodal EO.

title: Enhancing Fault Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks using Digital Twin and Predictive Maintenance
authors: S. Sharma; B. P. U. Ivy; M. Uppal; S. Mapari; D. Gupta; R. R
source_title: 2026 International Conference on AI-Driven Smart Systems and Ubiquitous Computing (ICAUC)
abstract: The emergence of Wireless Sensor Networks has enabled the detection of potentially dangerous or catastrophic events prior to their actual occurrence. Wireless Sensor Networks rely on sensors that collect data on environmental conditions, allowing an early warning system to be implemented for potentially dangerous or catastrophic events, enabling an organization to take actions to prevent or mitigate these types of events. The technology digital twin has potential to improve ability of a wireless sensor network to detect faults and recover from them before the fault occurs. Digital Twins are real-time representations of physical objects or systems that track activity and behaviour of that physical object or system. By combining the Digital Twin with a Wireless Sensor Network, it is possible to create a model of predictive maintenance that can detect potential fault conditions before they occur by utilizing fault-analysis techniques. By utilizing this model to improve the Wireless Sensor Network, it is possible to improve the reliability and reduce the incidence of natural disasters. This report describes how Digital Twins can be created and how they can be used in Predictive Maintenance to increase the reliability of wireless sensor networks. These findings illustrate the power of such an AI-based approach toward completely transforming fault management within WSNs, toward being more robust, efficient, and reliable sensor networks in today's world.

title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Service Life Prediction of Reinforced Concrete Under Real Environmental Actions
authors: Al Moubayed H.; Halawani H.; Altayabrrafei B.; Chendeb N.
source_title: International Conference on Computer and Applications, ICCA 2025 - Proceedings
abstract: We present a physics-informed, data-driven framework to predict the service life of reinforced concrete exposed to humidity, chloride corrosion, and freeze-thaw conditions. The approach combines performance-based descriptors (cover, apparent diffusion, chloride boundary and threshold, carbonation coefficient, freeze-thaw intensity) with in-situ sensing proxies (corrosion current, time of wetness) and trains regression and machine learning models to estimate service life. A synthetic but physics-consistent dataset (N=800) spanning urban, marine, and cold climates is released to enable reproducible evaluation. Gradient boosting delivers the best accuracy on a held-out test set, while feature importance confirms the dominance of physically meaningful variables. An ablation study shows that adding sensing features improves accuracy over physics-only inputs. Design curves illustrate actionable trade-offs: benefits of increasing cover saturate beyond about 60-70 mm, and service life decreases monotonically with freeze-thaw intensity. The framework supports optimizing design and material selection to meet target service life while reducing clinker content and embodied CO2. Beyond this contribution, future work will validate the model on multi-site field datasets and integrate it into digital twin platforms for continuous, uncertainty-aware monitoring of reinforced concrete structures. © 2025 IEEE.

title: Towards Artifacts-Based Behavior Modeling of Cyber-Physical Systems for Building Digital Twins
authors: B. Jacob; S. K. G
source_title: 2025 11th International Conference on Control, Automation and Robotics (ICCAR)
abstract: Behavior modeling of complex systems is a critical aspect in developing digital systems, such as Digital Twins (DT). It enables accurate representation of intricate dynamics and interactions, facilitating predictive capabilities that are essential for forecasting future states and behaviors. This paper presents a methodology for building predictive DTs of complex systems, addressing the critical challenge of behavior modeling. Our approach integrates data-driven techniques, including machine learning (ML), with physics-based or mathematical models, leveraging both real-time and historical data. We argue that this hybrid modeling strategy is essential for creating DTs capable of accurate prediction and “sliding forward in time” to visualize future system states. We propose a customizable framework that supports the development of a predictive maintenance module, covering physics/mathematics-based modeling, behavior learning, and uncertainty quantification. This framework is composed of programmable components derived from identified modeling artifacts, allowing for the seamless integration of diverse modeling techniques. Another key contribution of this work is the development of concrete modeling principles for designing predictive DTs, such as the principle of data-driven model calibration informed by physical constraints. We validate the effectiveness of our framework and principles through a case study that demonstrates the creation of a battery DT prototype. This is done for the battery of a laptop, utilizing real-time data collection and a discharge model to project battery discharge behavior. Our experiment highlights the potential of our approach for real-world applications in cyber-physical systems (CPS) by enabling proactive maintenance and improved system performance. Future work will extend this framework into a more sophisticated DT development environment following the artifactbased design presented here.

abstract: With the rapid development of smart manufacturing and automation technology, many factories have adopted autonomous inspection systems to enhance operational efficiency and safety. In particular, steel mills operate in extreme environments characterized by structural height variations, high temperatures, and heavy steel dust, making traditional manual inspections hazardous, labor-intensive, and inefficient. These challenges highlight the need for high-precision and automated inspection technologies. LiDAR-SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) has emerged as a key solution for industrial mapping and autonomous inspection. By constructing high-precision environmental models, LiDAR-SLAM enables inspection systems to perform positioning in complex, dynamic industrial environments with enhanced accuracy and stability. The robust localization framework provides a reliable foundation for autonomous inspection and precise positioning in steel product lines. This paper explores the application of LiDAR-SLAM technology for heavy industry inspections and its broader applications in industrial environments. The study demonstrates its potential to enhance inspection accuracy, improve workplace safety, and streamline operational management, contributing to the wider adoption of autonomous inspection systems in smart manufacturing.

title: Integrating Digital Twin and Random Survival Forests for Predicting Fatigue Behavior in Materials
authors: Jayani B.V.; Rajaram G.
source_title: 2025 International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Knowledge Economy, ICCIKE 2025
abstract: Fatigue failure poses a significant threat to the safety and reliability of mechanical systems, often leading to catastrophic and unpredictable outcomes. Traditional deterministic models and reactive maintenance strategies are inadequate for modern industrial applications, where assets are expected to operate continuously under varying loads and environmental conditions. The challenge is compounded by the prevalence of censored data, where the exact time of failure is unknown for many components. To address this critical need, this paper proposes a novel framework for a digital twin dedicated to prognostics and health management (PHM). Our methodology leverages the power of survival analysis, a statistical branch uniquely suited to modeling time-to-event data with censoring. We utilize a Random Survival Forest model to establish a probabilistic relationship between operational parameters and a component's remaining useful life (RUL). The model is trained on a comprehensive dataset, integrating physically-informed features to enhance its predictive capability. Through a rigorous cross-validation process, we demonstrate the robustness and generalization of our approach. The framework's performance is evaluated using key metrics that assess both its ability to rank components by their failure risk and the accuracy of its probabilistic predictions over time. The results indicate that the developed digital twin possesses an exceptional ability to differentiate between high and low-risk components and provides highly reliable survival probability curves. This capability enables a significant paradigm shift from reactive to proactive maintenance, allowing for the optimization of asset management, the reduction of unplanned downtime, and a marked improvement in system safety. The proposed framework provides a compelling and generalizable solution for building effective digital twins that can guide decision-making in real-world engineering applications. © 2025 IEEE.

title: A Comprehensive Review of Adaptive Traffic Management Systems for Sustainable Smart Cities
authors: Boopathi S.; Jothikumar R.
source_title: Proceedings of the 2025 International Conference on Computational Innovations and Sustainable Technologies, ICCIST 2025
abstract: Steep urbanization and rising car ownership have reinforced traffic congestion, leading to additional energy consumption and environmental pollution in cities. Classical fixed-time traffic control systems are inadequate for addressing dynamic and complex traffic modes because they do not respond promptly. This paper provides an extensive overview of Adaptive Traffic Management Systems (ATMS) highlighting the combination of Federated Learning (FL) and Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) as innovative enabling technologies for smart sustainable cities. FL provides privacy-preserving collaborative model training between distributed traffic nodes, while TinyML supports low-power real-time decision-making at the network edge. The convergence of these technologies creates better traffic flow, sharp cuts in carbon footprint, and reduced infrastructure energy requirements. We critically review recent implementations, point out significant research challenges like multi-modal integration and scalability issues, and provide future directions such as federated meta-learning, blockchain-protected architecture, and digital twin-based predictive control. Our results highlight the imperative role of FL and TinyML in building energy-saving, privacy-sensitive, and scalable ATMS according to United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). © 2025 IEEE.

title: MoveOD: Synthesizing Origin-Destination Commute Distribution from U.S. Census Data
authors: Sen R.; Talusan J.P.; Dubey A.; Mukhopadhyay A.; Samaranayake S.; Laszka A.
source_title: Proceedings - 17th ACM/IEEE International Conference on Cyber-Physical Systems, ICCPS 2026
abstract: High-resolution origin-destination (OD) tables are essential for a wide spectrum of intelligent transportation systems applications, from modeling traffic and signal timing optimization to congestion pricing and vehicle routing. However, outside a handful of data rich cities, such data is rarely available. We introduce MoveOD, an open-source pipeline that synthesizes public data into commuter OD flows with fine-grained spatial and temporal departure times for any county in the United States. MoveOD combines five open data sources - American Community Survey (ACS) departure time and travel time distributions, Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics (LODES) residence-to-workplace flows, county geometries, road network information from OpenStreetMap (OSM), and building footprints from OSM and Microsoft, into a single OD dataset. We use a constrained sampling and integer-programming method to reconcile the OD dataset with data from ACS and LODES. Our approach involves: (1) matching commuter totals per origin zone, (2) aligning workplace destinations with employment distributions, and (3) and calibrating travel durations to ACS-reported commute times. This ensures the OD data accurately reflects commuting patterns. We demonstrate the framework on Hamilton County, Tennessee, where we generate roughly 150,000 synthetic trips in minutes, which we feed into a digital-twin simulator with a benchmark suite of classical and learning-based vehicle-routing algorithms. The MoveOD pipeline is an end-to-end automated system, enabling users to easily apply it across the United States by giving only a county and a year; and it can be adapted to other countries with comparable census datasets. The source code to a lightweight browser dashboard will be made publicly available.  © 2026 IEEE.

authors: P. Almasan; S. Bakirtzis; J. Suárez-Varela; A. Lutu

abstract: Artificial intelligence-driven radio propagation models provide agile and robust solutions for mobile network operators in their effort to ensure the optimal performance of the wireless ecosystem and support its efficient expansion. In this paper, we introduce GraphWave, a neural graph-driven propagation solver hinging on the governing principles of ray tracing. The proposed model leverages a digitized version of the propagation environment to build a point cloud and extract an equivalent graph representation of the radio environment. By applying neural message passing over the equivalent graph, it allows the model to accurately infer radio-related quantities, e.g., received signal strength, in a three-dimensional environment. We showcase the use of GraphWave as a radio environment digital twin and we demonstrate that the model can learn from synthetic and real-world data while achieving low inference times.

abstract: The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in buildings holds immense potential for enhancing performance with respect to building efficiency or building sustainability. This paper systematically explores the literature in the intersection of IoT solutions, emerging digital technologies, sustainability, and Building Information Modelling. In this way, it sheds light on the state-of-the-art and the transformative potential of IoT and digital technologies in creating more sustainable buildings. While IoT systems are often used to improve various aspects of sustainability, the environmental sustainability of IoT systems themselves is rarely investigated. We therefore analyze the literature regarding the environmentally sustainable management of IoT devices employed. The analysis confirms a gap in the research in that IoT solutions are seen as a means to an end but are not the focus of sustainability considerations. Hence, it identifies the need for a sustainability-related Asset Management of IoT systems in buildings. It leads to the proposal of a corresponding implementation concept that bundles all the necessary IoT-related information of a building environment inside a Digital Twin. This establishes a comprehensive overview of the activities and properties of the IoT devices with applications in different use case scenarios, such as monitoring of operational states or insight into recycling potentials.

title: Intelligent Optimization of Manufacturing Supply Chains via Digital Twins and Deep Learning
authors: S. Ma; J. Qian
source_title: 2025 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Electrical, Automation and Computer Engineering (ICEACE)
abstract: Against the backdrop of volatile markets, this paper examines the collaborative optimization path of “perception-prediction-decision-feedback” within the manufacturing enterprise supply chain. This paper establishes an intelligent optimization system based on digital twins: IoT data is combined with a simulation core to create synchronized virtual and physical counterparts (Twin). Time series deep learning models (ARIMA, LSTM/optional TFT) are used to predict and analyze demand and inventory. Multi-objective intelligent optimization methods (improved particle swarm and ant colony algorithms) and robustness evaluation methods (FCE and Monte Carlo methods) are employed to achieve a closedloop decision-making process. The supply chain is transformed into a graphical model that reflects time changes, and a graph neural network (GNN) is implemented to measure the edge weights of the transportation network. The dynamic road conditions are combined with the order status to improve the path decision-making level. The public data of fresh food logistics in 2023 is analyzed and a simulation platform is built. The results show that the average delivery time is reduced by about 2.1 days, the on-time delivery rate of orders is increased by more than 12 percentage points, and the cost is reduced by nearly 20 percentage points. Even in the event of multiple interferences, self-recovery can be achieved within 8 hours. The combination of Twin+DL+dynamic optimization has effectively promoted the improvement of supply chain prediction accuracy, the strengthening of global collaboration and the enhancement of robustness, providing a replicable technical approach for the intelligent upgrade of the manufacturing industry.

title: Research on Intelligent Fault Diagnosis and Self-Healing Control for Smart Grids Based on Digital Twin
authors: Guo L.; Hu H.; Chen F.
source_title: 2025 7th International Conference on Energy Systems and Electrical Power, ICESEP 2025
abstract: As the structure of smart grids becomes increasingly complex, traditional fault handling methods face severe challenges in response speed and decision optimization. To address this issue, this paper proposes and constructs a framework for smart grid fault diagnosis and self-healing control based on digital twin technology. The core of this framework is a co-simulation-based multi-scale hybrid modeling method: an Electromagnetic Transient (EMT) model built with MATLAB/Simulink is capable of generating high-fidelity data, while an Electromechanical Transient (RMS) model developed in OpenDSS serves as a "decision-making sandbox"for the rapid deduction of multi-agent self-healing strategies. This study introduces a novel validation methodology where the digital twin is used to generate data for complex fault scenarios - such as high-impedance faults - that are poorly represented in standard datasets. Our CNN-LSTM fault diagnosis model, when augmented with this twin-generated data, demonstrates significantly improved robustness. In terms of fault diagnosis, the CNN-LSTM model designed in this study achieved an accuracy of 99.5% on a public benchmark dataset, with an average diagnosis time of only 26.1ms, striking a superior balance between performance and efficiency compared to other advanced algorithms. Building on this, the twin-inferred self-healing control strategy can complete fault isolation and restoration decisions within 2 seconds, increasing the system load recovery rate from 70% with traditional methods to 95% in typical scenarios. In summary, the digital twin framework proposed in this study provides an effective technical solution for the rapid and precise handling of grid faults, demonstrating its application potential in building future autonomous power systems. © 2025 IEEE.

abstract: INTRODUCTION: To address the urgent requirement for spatial safety distance monitoring in live-line work scenarios, traditional 2D vision methods often fail to provide accurate depth and physical spacing information. Furthermore, LiDAR point cloud processing in such environments faces severe challenges, including significant scale variations among targets (non-rigid dynamic human bodies vs. slender rigid utility poles), uneven point cloud density, and complex background occlusion. OBJECTIVES: This paper constructs a multi-category 3D point cloud dataset tailored for close-range live-line operation monitoring and proposes a lightweight improved 3D modeling and segmentation method based on PointNet++. METHODS: Building upon the fundamental hierarchical feature extraction framework, a Structure-Aware Feature Aggregation (SAFA) module is introduced during the decoding phase, utilizing a geometric curvature penalty term to enhance the continuity of reconstruction for slender poles and wires. Simultaneously, a dynamic density filtering and sampling strategy is integrated into the encoder to significantly improve the model's capability to capture critical parts, such as human extremities, in sparse regions. RESULTS: Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively enhances modeling accuracy and scene robustness for multi-scale targets while maintaining computational efficiency, achieving a mIoU of 87.5% and a Chamfer Distance of 3.68. CONCLUSION: This work provides reliable technical support for digital twins and spatial risk early warning in live-line operations. © 2026 IEEE.

abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities are advancing rapidly across the built-environment lifecycle, enabling computer vision-based progress and safety monitoring, predictive analytics, and digital twin-driven decision support. Despite these advances, AI adoption in construction and facility operations frequently stalls beyond pilot deployments due to fragmented stakeholder structures, high safety and liability exposure, unstable data pipelines, and persistent discontinuities between construction delivery and operational handover. Existing technology adoption models explain intention and use primarily through perceived usefulness and organizational readiness, but they remain insufficient for AI-enabled systems that introduce additional requirements related to trust calibration, explainability, cybersecurity and privacy, accountability, and continuous performance monitoring. This paper presents a framework-development and validationprotocol study for a governance-aware, lifecycle, multi-level adoption model for AI-enabled smart construction and facility operations. The model integrates classical adoption theory with trustworthy AI governance constructs and explicitly accounts for construction-to-operations handover continuity. Using a theory-driven integrative synthesis, the paper organizes determinants across five blocks-Technology & Data, Human & Trust, Organization & Governance, Ecosystem & Institutional, and Lifecycle/Handover-and specifies adoption outcomes across three stages: intention, implementation success, and continuance. Rather than claiming completed large-sample SEM results, the manuscript defines a multistakeholder survey design and a PLS-SEM/MGA reporting protocol, with optional Delphi-based refinement, to test lifecycle-contingent and role-specific effects in subsequent empirical work. The paper contributes a unified explanatory framework, a theory-grounded measurement instrument, and an actionable adoption readiness scorecard that supports safer, more sustainable, and scalable AI adoption across the builtenvironment lifecycle.  © 2026 IEEE.

authors: S. A. Al-Azazi; A. Ali; E. Al-Tayar; A. Ghaleb; F. Qasem; A. Saif

abstract: This paper presents an integrated workflow that combines building information modelling, digital twins, earlystage energy screening, and probabilistic project controls to support construction decisions that balance delivery risk and carbon performance. The study uses the open ENB2012 benchmark dataset of 768 simulated building design cases to train a surrogate model that predicts heating and cooling demand and enables rapid screening of envelope alternatives during concept development; accordingly, the reported numerical results should be interpreted as a reproducible proof-of-concept rather than project-specific performance estimates. A risk simulation model is then applied to a calibrated register of cost and schedule events under four levels of digital maturity, ranging from traditional delivery to governed use of building information modelling, digital twins, and generative artificial intelligence. Across 40,000 simulation iterations for each scenario, greater digital maturity consistently reduces average overruns and extreme outcomes, lowering the ninetieth percentile schedule delay from about 48 days to about 31 days and reducing mean cost overrun from about 10.8 percent to about 8.3 percent for a representative retrofit programme, while preserving the operational carbon benefits of envelope upgrades. The study contributes a transparent and reproducible decision framework that links information governance, design evaluation, and uncertainty analysis, and it concludes with a practical implementation pathway for organisations operating in resource-constrained environments.

abstract: Smart environments like smart cities and industrial facilities, as well as critical infrastructure, have become the inseparable parts of intelligent visual monitoring. This limitation is overcome in this paper through suggesting a Digital Twin-based reinforcement learning framework to adaptive and intelligent visual monitoring. The framework developed proposes the creation of a virtual digital twin of the real-life monitoring space, allowing continuous simulation, policy learning and safe optimization without interfering with the actual operations. A deep reinforcement learning agent can also be trained to optimize the best monitoring policies by combining monitoring accuracy, coverage, and energy use. Convolutional neural networks are used to extract visual features and a policy learning module is used to dynamically adapt the monitoring strategies according to environmental feedback. The CityFlow and VisDrone data is tested in an experimental environment simulating a digital twin. The suggested solution is more accurate in detection (95.8), lessening redundant visual processing (23.6), and more energy efficient (19.4) than the current monitoring baselines based on static monitoring. These findings indicate the success of digital twin-aided reinforcement learning to strengthen the adaptability, effectiveness, and robustness of smart visual devices.  © 2026 IEEE.

title: Exploring the Use of Building Information Modeling - Virtual Reality for Building Construction Progress Monitoring and Issue Detection: A Systematic Review

source_title: 2025 International Conference on Informatics, Multimedia, Cyber and Information System (ICIMCIS)
abstract: The construction industry, characterized by intricate workflows and persistent challenges in productivity and safety, is increasingly embracing digital transformation. Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Virtual Reality (VR), along with related Extended Reality (XR) technologies, are at the forefront of this shift. While existing literature acknowledges the potential of BIM-VR integration for visualization and collaboration, a critical synthesis specifically targeting its efficacy in construction progress monitoring and issue detection is lacking. Our systematic review reveals that BIM-VR/AR integration significantly enhances the accuracy and timeliness of progress tracking through immersive as-built vs. as-planned comparisons and facilitates proactive issue detection. Notably, this study proposes a novel conceptual framework that explicitly delineates the causal pathway between BIM-VR technological inputs (BIM model, VR/AR/XR interface, reality capture data), core processes (immersive visualization, automated data comparison), and project outcomes (enhanced monitoring accuracy, reduced rework), while quantifying the mediating effect of data interoperability on monitoring precision—a gap overlooked in prior studies. However, the reliability of these applications is constrained by underlying technical bottlenecks, including data interoperability issues, fidelity limitations in reality capture, and challenges in achieving robust on-site registration. Furthermore, widespread adoption is hampered by the high cost of hardware and a significant skills gap among the workforces. This review contributes a synthesized analysis of the state-of-the-art, a quantitative assessment of research trends, the aforementioned conceptual framework, and a critical discussion of challenges and future directions. The findings offer scholars a consolidated knowledge base and equip practitioners with evidence-based insights for strategic implementation.

abstract: Historic city centers in rapidly growing cities face interconnected challenges of climate vulnerability, development pressure, congestion, environmental decline, and heritage degradation. In Bandung, Indonesia, Alun-Alun Bandung is a strategic urban core where civic identity, religious activity, commerce, public space, and colonial-era heritage intersect, while also facing flooding, limited green open space, traffic pressure, heat island effects, and fragmented heritage management. This paper proposes a Digital Triplet-enabled regenerative planning framework for climate-resilient heritage city centers, using Alun-Alun Bandung as an embedded case study. The framework integrates Nature-Based Solutions (NBS), Transfer of Development Rights (TDR), and climate-responsive adaptive reuse of heritage buildings. Methodologically, the study applies a qualitative embedded case study supported by spatial observation, policy review, project-based urban design data, and scenario-based indicator assessment. The Digital Triplet is structured through physical, digital, and socio-governance layers, linking existing urban conditions, analytical modeling, and planning decision-making. Preliminary assessment indicates that NBS improves ecological performance, TDR supports conservation financing and development control, and adaptive reuse reduces demolition-related carbon impacts while strengthening historical identity. The study contributes to smart city and regenerative urbanism discourse by positioning Digital Triplet as a governance-oriented decision-support framework for heritage-sensitive climate adaptation in the Global South

title: Grammar-Guided Mechanism Discovery: From Process Data to Transferable Governing Equations
authors: X. Xu; H. -X. Li
source_title: 2026 16th International Conference on Information Science and Technology (ICIST)
abstract: Data-driven discovery of governing equations from spatiotemporal observations is a key step toward interpretable and transferable models of controlled dynamical systems. Existing methods face a fundamental trade-off: sparse-regression methods such as SINDy depend on predefined libraries and may miss localized or control-coupled mechanisms, whereas prior-free symbolic regression explores large expression spaces with limited use of domain knowledge. Our key idea is to replace term-level library selection with a typed mechanism grammar, which embeds engineering priors into candidate generation and constrains the search toward physically admissible mechanism compositions. Building on such grammar, we propose Grammar-MD (Grammar-guided Mechanism Discovery), a framework for discovering physically interpretable governing equations in controlled distributed parameter systems. Grammar-MD couples a neural surrogate for derivative estimation, a grammar-guided evolutionary search for mechanism-level candidate generation, and a validation-guided refinement step that identifies a compact active mechanism set. By recovering structured mechanisms rather than trajectory-specific correlations, Grammar-MD is designed to generalize beyond the control inputs used for identification. Experiments on a controlled one-dimensional distributed parameter system demonstrate perfect mechanism-family recovery across a 0%–10% noise sweep, while maintaining reliable term-level identification and coefficient estimation as noise increases. The discovered governing equation also rolls out accurately under unseen control profiles, highlighting the potential of Grammar-MD for interpretable digital twin development.

title: LF-SA Based Solar Cell Parameter Extraction for Floating Photovoltaic Systems
authors: V. Abhinav Kumar; A. Goswami; P. K. Sadhu; S. Bhattacharya
source_title: 2025 International Conference on Power Electronics and Energy (ICPEE)
abstract: The floating photovoltaic (FPV) systems installed in saltwater areas have distinct difficulties with solar cell parameter recovery owing to the corrosive effect of salt-mist, changing temperature, and dynamic operating circumstances that distort IV characteristic. Conventional metaheuristic methods of single-diode model (SDM) fitting can be accused of premature convergence and low accuracy with noisy and time-varying data. In this paper, a hybrid optimization technique combining Levy flight (LF) exploration with Simulated Annealing (SA) exploitation is proposed in order to obtain better accuracy and robustness of the parameter extraction. The LF-SA model is mathematically modeled to fit SDM, tested on artificial and benchmark I-V data, and compared to Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and standalone SA. Findings indicate that there is an increase of $\mathbf{1 5}-\mathbf{2 5 \%}$ in the estimation accuracy and minimized RMSE with no decrease in the computational efficiency that is compatible with embedded monitoring. The method also identifies the indicators of degradation, including resistance building up due to salt intrusion, and assists with predictive maintenance in FPV systems. Such results demonstrate that LF-SA is an encouraging optimization tool towards dependable model of the solar cells and real-time health of offshore PV systems.

title: From CAD to POMDP: Probabilistic Planning for Robotic Disassembly of End-of-Life Products
authors: J. Baumgärtner; M. Hansjosten; D. Hald; A. Hauptmannl; A. Puchta; J. Fleischer
source_title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: To support the circular economy, robotic systems must not only assemble new products but also disassemble end-of-life (EOL) ones for reuse, recycling, or safe disposal. Existing approaches to disassembly sequence planning often assume deterministic and fully observable product models, yet real EOL products frequently deviate from their initial designs due to wear, corrosion, or undocumented repairs. We argue that disassembly should therefore be formulated as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP), which naturally captures uncertainty about the product’s internal state. We present a mathematical formulation of disassembly as a POMDP, in which hidden variables represent uncertain structural or physical properties. Building on this formulation, we propose a task and motion planning framework that automatically derives specific POMDP models from CAD data, robot capabilities, and inspection results. To obtain tractable policies, we approximate this formulation with a reinforcement-learning approach that operates on stochastic action outcomes informed by inspection priors, while a Bayesian filter continuously maintains beliefs over latent EOL conditions during execution. Using three products on two robotic systems, we demonstrate that this probabilistic planning framework outperforms deterministic baselines in terms of average disassembly time and variance, generalizes across different robot setups, and successfully adapts to deviations from the CAD model, such as missing or stuck parts.

title: Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning for Secure Cloud Scheduling with Digital Twin Validation
authors: Gadani N.N.; Anjaria R.
source_title: 14th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications, ICRERA 2025
abstract: Cloud-based time-critical smart grid applications need to be able to efficiently schedule resources to maintain their performance and robustness in the presence of time varying loads and cyber intrusions. In fact, we find that simple heuristics as Round-Robin (RR) and Least-Loaded (LL) are not viable choices in adversarial settings and that single-layer DRL architectures cannot scale well and are not stable. To enable attack-aware and efficient performance scheduling, this work introduces a Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning (HDRL) based structure along with a digital twin (DT) validation environment. In the HDRL model, local and global PPO agents work in sync to allocate resources at various levels and DT orchestrates redundancy of workloads and cyberattacks injection for resilience purposes. The assessment was performed on actual building load traces with normal, low attack, and high attack profiles. The results indicate that HDRL outperforms the baselines in terms of throughput, SLA violations and recovery time. Under high attack, HDRL also exhibited a reduction in SLA violations of more than 50% relative to LL and RR as well as 50% decrease in the time needed for recovery. Using Wilcoxon signed-rank test, we statistically validate that the improvements by HDRL are indeed significant with adversarial workloads. These results conclude HDRL with DT validation to be a novel and viable approach to secure, resilient, and flexible scheduling in the cloud for smart grid applications. © 2025 IEEE.

title: Robotics and Automation for Sustainable Systems: Autonomous Robots, Smart Manufacturing, Sensing, and Environmental Automation
authors: Arathi A.; Vishwakarma S.K.

abstract: Moving towards Industry 5.0 from Industry 4.0 entails building robotic systems that are not just efficient, but also explicitly sustainable. Although autonomous robots, digital twins, and intelligent manufacturing processes separately show improvements in efficiency or energy usage, there still does not exist any holistic framework that concurrently considers closed loop multi-agent sensing, lifecycle carbon footprint assessment, and manufacturing processes. This paper proposes a unified framework for building a sustainability-aware robotic system that integrates (i) Energy-Carbon Aware Active Sensing (ECAS) multi-agent planner, (ii) a sustainability-focused digital twin incorporating LCA models, and (iii) cross domain coordination framework that incorporates environmental sensing along with manufacturing processes.Sustainability aware autonomous robotics is modeled as a stochastic optimal control problem where the goal is to minimize energy and time varying carbon intensity while simultaneously optimizing information gain. The proposed controller employs a receding-horizon optimization strategy to adapt robotic activity according to dynamic carbon intensity and information gain. We evaluate our model using simulation, experimentation, and field tests in a 2 km2 environment monitoring setting. Our results indicate a decrease of up to 50% in energy per task and 20-40% reduction in CO2e per mapped area over baseline planners with significant improvement (p < 0.01). Our work demonstrates a concrete step towards designing explicitly sustainable robotic systems.  © 2026 IEEE.

title: Integrating Intelligent Fault Recovery Mechanisms into Real-Time System Software for Resilient Embedded Application Design
authors: K. Santhosh; E. Boddepalli; S. G; V. Waiker; S. Thawkar; A. Balakumar
source_title: 2026 3rd International Conference on Trends in Engineering Systems and Technologies (ICTEST)
abstract: Embedded systems used in real-time applications-such as aerospace, healthcare, and industrial automation-must operate continuously and reliably, even in the presence of unexpected faults. Traditional fault-tolerance techniques, such as watchdog timers, static redundancy, and checkpoint/restart methods, often suffer from delayed recovery, high resource consumption, and limited adaptability to dynamic fault conditions. These limitations hinder the resilience and real-time performance of embedded systems, especially in complex and resource-constrained environments. This research proposes an intelligent fault recovery framework that integrates adaptive machine learning-based fault detection and autonomous recovery mechanisms directly into real-time system software. The methodology involves collecting fault data from testbeds and fault injection tools, training predictive models using decision trees and LSTM networks, and embedding these models into the real-time operating system (RTOS). Reinforcement learning is employed to optimize recovery actions dynamically based on system state and context. The system was evaluated through controlled experiments involving synthetic and real-world fault scenarios. Results demonstrate significant improvements in fault detection accuracy, reduced recovery latency, and minimal deadline violations compared to conventional methods. The proposed approach enhances system resilience without compromising real-time constraints, offering a robust solution for building self-healing embedded systems capable of intelligent fault management in critical applications.

This is the direct solution to one of the major wind turbine fault prediction challenges: the lack of actual fault data. By generating high-volume, balanced, and labelled training data, the framework facilitates building of quality machine learning models that would otherwise prove extremely hard to develop on actual turbine operations. The framework demonstrates a total end-to-end pipeline physics driven data generation verified through successful machine learning deployment compared to actual operational data of an NREL 5-MW reference wind turbine. abstract: This paper tackles the challenge of automating facility inspections by detecting building components, estimating their six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) poses (position and orientation), and comparing these estimations to Building Information Modeling (BIM) ground truth data. Vision based Deep learning methods offer promising results in pose estimation. They rely heavily on large annotated image datasets for training, which are often lacking or too specific for building settings. Manually annotating large datasets is both labor-intensive and time-consuming, particularly when they contain hundreds of images. This challenge further underscores the need for efficient and automated methods for dataset annotation, particularly in building environments where dataset size and complexity are significant. We present a study examining the point where the performance of a 6-DoF object detection algorithm is efficient. In particular, we analyze the proportion of real data required for detection and pose estimation models to perform well on double-leaf doors. Synthetic data are generated using the Digital Twin (DT), which is intended to serve as the future reference for BIM in facility inspections. Adding synthetic data reduces rotation error by up to 1.7°, starting from 1,000 images. We analyze the effectiveness of different proportions of real and synthetic data to provide insight into optimizing dataset composition. The accuracy of the 3D center point and the accuracy at 25 cm/25 degrees are better than 90% accuracy when more than 50 real images combined with synthetic data. © 2025 IEEE.

abstract: Building Information Modeling (BIM) plays a key role in organizing geometric and semantic information extracted from indoor 3D point clouds, supporting applications such as facility management, renovation, and smart building operations. Despite extensive research on scan-to-BIM, most existing review studies focus on isolated processing stages or specific techniques, rather than presenting the workflow as an integrated process. To address this limitation, this paper presents a thorough review of indoor scan-to-BIM reconstruction methods by integrating bibliometric analysis with a systematic technical review. The bibliometric analysis examines global research trends in scan-to-BIM studies and explores keyword network relationships. The study reviews the complete scan-to-BIM workflow, including room segmentation, element segmentation, reconstruction of structural and non-structural components, opening recognition, and BIM modeling. Both traditional geometric methods and recent deep learning-based approaches are analyzed and compared. The review also discusses current challenges and identifies future research directions to support further automation and robustness in scan-to-BIM approaches. This paper offers a clear synthesis of existing research and provides practical insights that can guide future developments toward more effective and automated indoor scan-to-BIM systems.

abstract: Reconstructing high-fidelity 3D building models from UAV imagery is essential for large-scale digital twin development. To address this, we propose a semantic edge regularization framework that supervises 3DGS to produce crisp architectural boundaries. During training, we align rendered image gradients with these extracted edges, forcing the Gaussians to converge into sharp structural geometries. Evaluations across campus environments, dense urban centers, and custom residential datasets demonstrate significant improvements in edge fidelity without requiring architectural modifications to the 3DGS pipeline. title: An end to end workflow for synthetic data generation for robust object detection*
authors: J. Metzler; F. Bahrpeyma; D. Reichelt
source_title: 2023 IEEE 21st International Conference on Industrial Informatics (INDIN)
abstract: Object detection is a task in computer vision that involves detecting instances of visual objects of a particular class in digital images. Numerous computer vision tasks highly depend on object detection such as instance segmentation, image captioning and object tracking. A major purpose of object detection is to develop computational models that provide inputs crucial to computer vision applications. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have recently become popular due to their key roles in enabling object detection. However, the performance of CNNs is largely dependent upon the quality and quantity of training datasets, which are often difficult to obtain in real-world applications. In order to ensure the robustness of such models, it is vital that training instances are provided under various randomized conditions. These conditions are typically a combination of a variety of factors, including lighting conditions, object location, the presence of multiple objects in the scene, varieties of backgrounds, and the angle of the camera. In particular, companies, depending on their applications (such as fault detection, anomaly detection, condition monitoring, predictive quality and so on), require specialized models for their custom products and so always face difficulties in providing a large number of randomized conditioned instances of their objects. The primary reason is that the process of capturing randomized conditioned images of real objects is usually costly, time-consuming, and challenging in practice. Due to the efficiency gained so far via the use of synthetic data for training such systems, synthetic data has recently attracted considerable attention. This paper presents an end-to-end synthetic data generation method for building a robust object detection model for customized products using NVIDIA Omniverse and CNNs. In this paper, we demonstrate and evaluate our contribution to the modeling of chess pieces, where a total accuracy of 98.8 % was obtained.

abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive systematic literature review (SLR) investigating the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in advancing Circular Economy (CE) practices across diverse industries from 2015 to 2025. Starting with an initial dataset of 815 articles retrieved exclusively from the Scopus database, a systematic screening process based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria reduced the collection to 335 studies. Following a thorough quality evaluation and relevance assessment, a final sample of 49 articles was selected for analysis. The review encompasses a diverse range of application domains, including manufacturing, waste management, energy systems, and supply chains. It further identifies the targeted CE strategies enabled by these AI applications, such as resource optimization, waste reduction, product life extension, and emission mitigation. Building upon this synthesis, the study proposes a robust conceptual framework designed to facilitate the strategic integration of AI technologies within CE initiatives. Based on the analysis of the final sample of 49 papers, the proposed framework offers actionable design implications. It identifies critical innovation pathways to support the development of intelligent and sustainable CE solutions. By combining theoretical foundations with empirical evidence, this research advances AI-enabled sustainability and promotes the development of intelligent systems for sustainable circular transformation.

title: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance in Industry 4.0: A Systematic Review and Research Directions
authors: H. Cherradi; K. Benjilali; A. Elasri; S. Hamida; B. Cherradi; O. Bouattane
source_title: 2026 6th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM) has emerged as a cornerstone of Industry 4.0, enabling data-driven decisionmaking to minimize downtime and optimize asset lifecycle management. Even though PdM tasks, such as anomaly detection and prescriptive maintenance, are increasingly using artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, the field is still fragmented across algorithms, evaluation procedures, and industrial contexts. In order to address this, we use VOSviewer to perform a systematic bibliometric analysis of 3.247 peer-reviewed publications from 2020 to 2025. The results show that there are four main research clusters: domain-specific applications, condition-based diagnostics, core AI methodologies, and Industry 4.0 infrastructure. Finally, we propose a unifying taxonomy in the Industry 4.0 stack that interconnects AI techniques to PdM applications, while also discussing the potential of explainability, human-AI cooperation and multitask learning as well as the crucial problems of generalizability, data-availability and lack of business justification. We believe this study provides a systematic architecture to equip scholars and practitioners with better insights to pursue the next step toward the building blocks of robust, interpretable and applicable PdM solutions.

title: Real-Time Adaptive Gray-Box Digital Twin for Industrial Equipment: Online Calibration and Edge-Deployable Prediction
authors: Wen X.; Wen C.
source_title: 2026 11th International Symposium on Advances in Electrical, Electronics and Computer Engineering, ISAEECE 2026
abstract: Industrial assets frequently experience parameter drift during operation, which degrades predictive models and inflates maintenance costs. Because purely data-driven models struggle with covariate shift and physics-based models accumulate approximation biases, this paper proposes a Minimal Gray-Box Digital Twin for real-time condition monitoring and adaptive state prediction in embedded systems. The architecture integrates an interpretable state-space backbone, an online Extended Kalman Filter and Recursive Least Squares layer for training-free parameter tracking, and a lightweight residual neural network to capture unmodeled nonlinearities, structurally guided by a threeterm error decomposition strategy. Validated across three physical simulation benchmarks and a real-world building energy dataset, the proposed method yields statistically significant performance gains with a p-value less than 0.01. Crucially, the model achieves a rapid recovery of 20 plus or minus 19 steps and an ultra-low latency of 54.6 microseconds per step on an edge-class CPU. Utilizing merely 4500 neural parameters and approximately 2 megabytes of memory, the proposed framework presents a highly efficient, embedded-ready alternative to computationally demanding Physics-Informed Neural Networks and deep learning approaches that rely on runtime gradient updates.  © 2026 IEEE.

abstract: Building-based energy efficiency levels in five cities located in different climate zones of Turkey (Erzurum, Antalya, Rize, Istanbul, and Gaziantep) were analyzed using the fuzzy logic method. For each city, multi-criteria variables such as thermal insulation quality, annual energy consumption, building age, and user energy awareness were evaluated, and corresponding energy efficiency scores were calculated. According to the results, Istanbul demonstrated high energy efficiency, Antalya and Rize showed moderate efficiency, while Erzurum and Gaziantep exhibited low efficiency. Uncertainty-based systems like fuzzy logic offer a flexible means of evaluating complex relationships between multiple variables in smart cities. Moreover, the identification of regions with low efficiency paves the way for the development of policies such as urban transformation, public awareness campaigns, and the integration of innovative technologies. In this regard, climate-specific energy solutions tailored to each city play a critical role in achieving the sustainability goals of smart city planning. This study emphasizes the necessity of considering regional differences in energy efficiency in the implementation of smart city applications.

title: Comparative study of indoor and outdoor building point cloud model registration based on ICP algorithm and NDT algorithm
authors: Cheng Y.
source_title: 2026 6th International Symposium on Computer Technology and Information Science, ISCTIS 2026
abstract: Due to the different data collection channels and equipment for indoor and outdoor building point cloud models, the models constructed have certain differences in spatial position, size, and angle. As a key technology connecting the real world and digital twin, the automatic registration of indoor and outdoor building point cloud models has become a research hotspot of multiple cutting-edge interdisciplinary fields. In this paper, the ICP algorithm and NDT algorithm were used to register 3 sets of the indoor and outdoor architectural models generated automatically. Overlap RMSE, registration consistency, and inwardness were used as the evaluation indicators for the registration effect. Recognizing that standard geometric metrics often fail to detect structural anomalies, we propose an "inwardness"score designed to identify physical penetration artifacts. Our experimental evidence reveals a critical vulnerability in NDT: while it achieves marginally lower overlap RMSE, it suffers from severe target-surface penetration, yielding an inwardness score below 0.5. ICP, conversely, demonstrates superior robustness, successfully maintaining the physical integrity of the interior model. These findings validate inwardness as an indispensable evaluation metric for low-overlap registration tasks. © 2026 IEEE.

abstract: On-site construction and renovation remain among the least productive and most resource-intensive industrial activities due to labour-intensive workflows, limited digital integration, and dynamic site conditions. Unlike industrial robots in structured factories or disaster robots in unstructured environments, construction robots operate in semi-structured sites with evolving geometry, incomplete digital information, and continuous human presence, creating both deployment challenges and automation opportunities. This paper reviews on-site construction robotics with emphasis on digital workflow integration and field performance. Existing research is organised into three application domains-assembly and placement, inspection and mapping, and drilling and surface operations-and analysed through a digital workflow stack including BIM-to-robot execution, simulation-informed planning, digital twins for closed-loop coordination, and perception-semantic integration. Reported deployments are synthesised using performance indicators such as cycle time, setup efficiency, geometric accuracy, rework reduction, ergonomic workload, and resource efficiency. Key barriersincluding perception robustness, interoperability, safety assurance, and workforce adaptation-are discussed to outline research directions for scalable and sustainable construction robotics.

authors: B. C. Hopkins; R. Hartzell; E. J. Paul; C. Hinkle; C. Yuroff; C. Dreyer; F. Zhu
abstract: Planetary surface missions depend on reliable rover traversability across diverse terrain conditions. Accurate prediction of traversability relies on terramechanics, the study of wheel-soil interactions, which links terrain properties to vehicle dynamics. Building and validating terramechanics-based models require high-fidelity datasets that couple specific rover geometries with well-characterized surface topographies, yet such datasets remain sparse or incomplete. This paper presents a streamlined experimental pipeline for generating and disseminating comprehensive mobility datasets. We describe our rover, test campaigns, and detail the data-acquisition architecture. Additionally, we release a publicly accessible repository of rover state & action time series, wheel imagery, and terrain scans captured in the Mines Lunar Surface Simulator. The dataset and methodology enable rapid development and validation of traversability metrics, digital twin simulation, and system identification.

abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly used for surveillance and monitoring in urban environments, where effective obstacle avoidance is critical for safe and effi-cient operations. This paper presents a LiDAR-based obstacle avoidance system using the 3D Vector Field Histogram Plus (3D VFH+) method, implemented on the Field-based Autonomous LiDAR Control for Obstacle Navigation (FALCON), an in-house UAV developed at Ulster University. The study focuses on UAV navigation around the university campus, specifically York Street, where buildings pose significant challenges for real-time obstacle avoidance. A digital twin model of FALCON is used for simulation and validation, integrating 3D VFH + with a proportional integral derivative (PID) control strategy optimised using particle swarm optimisation (PSO), genetic algorithm (GA) and Mayfly algorithm (MA). The system is tested in a simulated environment including the Ulster University Belfast (UUB) campus, comparing different PID tuning methods in terms of path deviation, stability, and obstacle clearance. Results demonstrate that PSO and GA-optimised PID controllers provide smoother trajectories and improved stability, ensuring safe UAV navigation in complex urban settings. This research contributes to the development of robust UAV obstacle avoidance strategies for urban surveillance and monitoring applications.  © 2025 IEEE.

title: Urban Building Updates Monitoring Based on Sky Visibility Estimation From Satellite Signals
authors: H. Xu; G. Zhang; L. -T. Hsu
abstract: As the digital twins for the urban area, 3-D building models have been applied in many areas and their reliability has become more and more vital. In a fast-developing city, the scale of construction renewal is usually tremendous with a high frequency, which makes the existing 3-D building models easy to be out-of-date and introduces errors. In this article, we proposed a monitoring algorithm for building updates based on satellite signals. We use satellite measurements to estimate the sky visibility from building blockages. By comparing it to the sky visibility from the existing data set, we can obtain the direction of the building being updated. Finally, the building update directions detected from multiple agents are collaborated in a crowd-sourcing manner to estimate the overall update probability of buildings. A simulation and a real experiment are conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm. The proposed monitoring algorithm is robust to sky visibility estimation accuracy, number of agents, and agent positioning error from the simulation analysis. In the real experiment, the building with updates can be accurately detected by the satellite measurements collected from a short pedestrian trajectory around this area.

abstract: The rapid growth of edge computing has enabled low-latency and high-efficiency processing for a wide range of applications; however, it also leads to significant energy consumption and carbon emissions. In this context, this study investigates a CO2 emission minimization problem in a digital twin-aided edge computing system, aiming to optimize task offloading decisions, transmit power, and processing rates of Internet of Things (IoT) devices. To address the formulated mixed-integer nonlinear programming problem, we propose two solutions: 1) an alternating optimization method based on the successive convex approximation framework and 2) a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approach. Extensive simulations validate the effectiveness of the proposed solutions, demonstrating significant reductions in CO2 emissions, robust optimization performance, and superior results compared to benchmark schemes. The findings highlight the feasibility of integrating advanced optimization and artificial intelligence-driven techniques to achieve environmentally sustainable and high-performance edge computing systems, paving the way for greener technological innovation.

abstract: Abstract-This article presents a cost-effective framework for indoor localization that integrates spherical panoramas, smartphone cameras, and building information modeling (BIM). PPE-AM provides an initial pose estimate by matching attributes extracted from the panorama with those rendered from the BIM. PPE-GA refines this estimate using a genetic algorithm (GA) that aligns semantic and depth maps. Our approach eliminates the need for premapping and on-site data collection, offering a practical alternative to expensive solutions such as spherical panorama localization based on point cloud or 3-D line maps. Smartphone pose estimation (SPE), leveraging the localized panoramas, achieved a mean 3-D error of 0.92 m. The proposed framework offers a robust and scalable solution for accurate indoor localization, with potential applications in augmented reality, facility management, and digital twin technologies.  © 2001-2012 IEEE.

abstract: Multi-sensor fusion of LiDAR and cameras plays a crucial role in advancing technologies such as environmental perception and 3-D reconstruction in autonomous vehicles and robotic systems.
